newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat opposition leader hurt in machinegun attack.
newsitem.headline: Croat opposition leader hurt in machinegun attack.

text.p: A Bosnian Croat opposition leader and his wife were wounded in a machinegun attack on their home in Mostar, the European Union mission in the gangster-ridden city said on Tuesday.

An EU statement said unidentified assailants opened fire from a car on the home of moderate coalition leader Jole Musa at 11:20 p.m. on Monday in the western half of Mostar, which is ruled by Croat ultra-nationalists.
"Both Mr Musa and his wife were injured in the attack. Mr Musa required hospital treatment," the statement said.

HINA, the Croatian state news agency, said Musa -- who is in advanced middle age -- was expected to undergo surgery for a wound in the groin. His condition was not life-threatening, it quoted doctors as saying.
Western European Union police and the loosely united Moslem-Croat police force they oversee had begun an investigation.

The special EU envoy, Sir Martin Garrod, deplored the attack on Musa. He heads a two-year-old mission working to reunite sectors of Mostar held by Moslem and Croat nationalists who ripped apart the city in war.
"Sir Martin expresses serious concern about the possible consequences of this attack on the process of normalisation in Mostar," the EU statement said.
"He urges leaders at all levels to do their utmost to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice as soon as possible."

Analysts said the perpetrators were probably right-wing paramilitary gangsters who pervade the Croat power structure in Mostar and are hostile to Musa's platform of reconciliation and power-sharing with Moslems.
Musa won a parliamentary seat in Bosnia's September 14 general elections that were prescribed by the 1995 Dayton peace treaty to help reunify a country torn apart in 43 months of nationalist war.
A joint city council was formed in Mostar in August after Croat nationalists scrapped a post-election boycott to avert Western sanctions, but the new governing body is toothless.

Musa headed a Mostar-area slate of five moderate opposition parties against the dominant Croat nationalist HDZ party and the Moslem nationalist SDA, which took big majorities in their respective fiefdoms.
